I farm 16.9 mu here in Quzhou. My main crop is cotton like most folks around here, but I also plant some maize for the household and to sell a bit. Let me think about this year.

For cotton, I will put about 10 mu. Last year I planted Bt cotton — the seed dealer in town sells bags of good hybrid seed, everyone around here uses it because the bollworm doesn't eat it so bad. I will plough the land first in spring, the soil here is heavy and needs turning. For fertilizer, I do what my brother-in-law does — one bag of compound fertilizer (25 kg, 15-15-15) as base per mu, then urea at flowering. That gives me about 12 kg nitrogen per mu, 8 phosphorus, 8 potassium. Cotton needs water — I will irrigate from the well 3 times, at budding, flowering, and boll-filling. Even with Bt seed I still spray — aphids and spider mites don't care about Bt. I will spray maybe 6 times over the season. Last year I got about 260 kg seed cotton per mu, I hope for same.

For maize, 6.9 mu. I plant spring maize, hybrid seed — Zhengdan type from the dealer. Maize eats more nitrogen than cotton. I put about 18 kg N per mu, 6 P, 5 K. One base dressing with compound, then urea topdressing at big trumpet stage. Rotary tillage is enough for maize. Irrigate 2 times — planting and tasseling. Spray once or twice for corn borer. I usually get around 550 kg per mu.

Every bag of fertilizer costs real money, so I don't waste, but I don't skimp either — a bad harvest costs more than an extra bag.
